key_insight: ModHarness-RL treats an AI agent’s harness—the software that controls what interaction history and guidance it receives—as a learnable program rather than a fixed scaffold. The harness can evolve as the model trains.
problem_solved: Hand-written, fixed harnesses may not remain suitable across domains, datasets, or stages of model training, limiting how well they support agentic reinforcement learning.
method: Represent the agent harness as programs rather than a permanently fixed set of rules.
Learn harness programs from data to adapt the agent’s interaction context and guidance.
Evolve the harness alongside model training; the supplied abstract is truncated and does not specify the optimization procedure.
impact: This approach could help practitioners adapt agent scaffolding to changing model capabilities instead of relying solely on manual design. The supplied abstract does not report experimental results, so performance gains cannot be assessed.
visual_elements: Side-by-side diagram: fixed hand-written harness versus learnable, evolving harness.

Three input icons—domain, data, and model—feeding into harness adaptation.
paper_title: ModHarness-RL: Recasting Harnesses as Learnable and Evolving Programs for Agentic RL
paper_authors: Zelin He, Siyu Zhu, Jacob Helwig, Yujian Liu, Li An
